title: GPGME double-free vulnerability CVE-2026-129975
summary: GnuPG disclosed a critical double-free bug triggered by crafted OpenPGP user IDs, with data exfiltration possible and remote code execution not excluded. GPGME 2.3.1 and updated Gpg4win packages were released; deployment across dependent applications remains unverified.
fix: GPGME 2.3.1 released; updated Gpg4win 5.1.2 and backport patch available.

rootCause.summary: Buffer reallocation left a stale pointer in the context when status-line or key-listing reads returned early, resulting in a second free on context destruction.

history.summary: GnuPG disclosed CVE-2026-129975, a crafted long OpenPGP user ID double-free in GPGME, and warned of potential exfiltration and possible code execution.
GPGME 2.3.1, Gpg4win 5.1.2 and a backport patch were published. Installations still need to apply the fix.
